title: First salary and account setup
oneLiner: Set up salary banking so the first pay-cheque lands somewhere sensible.
goal: Establish what the offer actually pays and when, and set up an account structure that separates spending from saving before the first credit arrives.

stages.goal: Find out where they are: offer in hand, joined, or first credit already landed. Those are three answers, so ask with `quick_replies`: `Offer in hand`, `Already joined`, `First salary has landed`.
stages.exitWhen: The stage of the transition is known.

stages.goal: Read the offer and separate fixed monthly pay from variable, bonus and deductions. Show what you read, then hand back with `quick_replies`: `That matches my offer`, `The figures are different`.
stages.exitWhen: Fixed monthly take-home is established or explicitly unknown.

stages.goal: Propose a simple split - spending, short-term saving, buffer - as amounts, not percentages of a number they do not have yet. Ask whether it fits with `quick_replies`: `That split works`, `Change the amounts`, `Not now`.
Match the structure to real catalogue accounts, checking eligibility honestly. Offer `quick_replies` naming the accounts you matched, plus `Neither of these`.
stages.exitWhen: Products are matched or the gap is stated.

stages.goal: Prepare one proposal, or save the plan for when they join.
stages.exitWhen: A proposal or a saved plan exists.

mustEstablish: Fixed monthly pay, separated from variable and bonus. This is the single most common place to go wrong.
Whether relocation or a deposit will consume the first month or two.
Whether the employer mandates a particular bank.
neverDo: Never treat CTC as take-home. Never treat a variable bonus as monthly income.
Do not bundle. One account and at most one savings instrument is the right answer for a first job.
Do not commit them to a recurring deposit amount from a salary that has not arrived yet.
Do not check eligibility against a number the customer guessed.

objectionPaths.respondBy: Accept it immediately. Help with the structure regardless - the split matters more than where it sits.

objectionPaths.signal: does not want to commit to saving yet
objectionPaths.respondBy: Reasonable before the first credit. Save the plan with a review date and stop.

completion.default: The next action is explicit: prepare the chosen salary account or starter saving proposal, or save the split-and-review plan until the first credit arrives.
completion.nivedita: Unusual - likely asking for a grandchild. The next action is a general first-salary checklist, without pulling her own accounts into it.
completion.rhea: Likely a family member's first job. The next action is a shareable account-and-savings structure, keeping her own position separate unless she brings it in.
completion.ravi: His core journey. The next action is a confirmation-ready starter structure after resolving the offer-letter/addendum pay conflict, with a monthly figure small enough to survive a bad month.

openers: I have just started my first job - how should I set up my banking?
My salary lands next month and I want it to go somewhere sensible
How much of my pay should I be putting aside?
